guides.title: Discovery brief
guides.question: How do I turn an incomplete first conversation into a one-page brief that names the decision, the people, the constraints and what is still unknown?
guides.summary: A one-page brief that separates attributed facts from assumptions and unknowns, ranks the questions that change the design, and proposes one bounded next step with named acceptors.

guides.title: Stakeholder map
guides.question: Who can fund, accept, operate or block this outcome, what does each of them need to see, and which conversation comes next?
guides.summary: A revisable map of interests, influence and evidence needs per person, with the next conversation planned for each and the conflicts named rather than resolved on paper.

guides.title: Requirements contract
guides.question: How do I write functional and nonfunctional requirements so that each one has a population, a measurement and a named acceptor before anything is built?
guides.summary: A testable contract of functional and nonfunctional requirements, tiered and attributed, with an acceptance row per requirement and the assumptions it rests on stated.

guides.title: Architecture decision record
guides.question: How do I record an architecture choice so that its options, assumptions and tradeoffs are visible and the evidence that would reverse it is stated?
guides.summary: A decision record that compares defensible options in the same terms, dates every assumption, writes tradeoffs as consequences and names what would reverse the choice.

guides.title: Request-path map
guides.question: For one concrete request, which piece of compute, storage, identity and network is responsible at each hop, who owns it, and what failure would I see there?
guides.summary: A hop-by-hop map of one request through authoring, control plane, compute, storage and result delivery, with owners, trust boundaries, cloud-specific names marked confirmed or not, and the failure each hop would show.

guides.title: Access review
guides.question: Which principal may take which action on which object, and how do I prove the denials as well as the allows with representative identities?
guides.summary: A principal, object and action matrix with a reason per allow, negative tests executed first with captured errors, and untested cells recorded as gaps rather than passes.

guides.title: Compute choice
guides.question: Given this workload's pattern, observed concurrency, latency tolerance and operational limits, which compute should it run on and what evidence would change that?
guides.summary: A per-workload compute decision derived from pattern, observed concurrency and latency tolerance, with operational limits, assumptions and the observations that would overturn it.

guides.title: Ingestion decision
guides.question: What can each source actually expose, what freshness and replay does the decision need, who owns each side, and which ingestion pattern follows from that?
guides.summary: A source-first ingestion decision comparing snapshot, watermark, change capture, file drop and managed connector patterns on what each needs, misses and costs, with owners and conditions attached.

guides.title: Change-data contract
guides.question: Which keys identify an entity and a delivery, what orders its changes, what counts as a deletion, a duplicate or a conflict, and what happens to each?
guides.summary: A contract naming keys, ordering, deletions, duplicate classes and a conflict policy, with a target shape and a hand-authored test sequence the resolver must reproduce.

guides.title: Quality response plan
guides.question: When a record fails a check, where does it go, who owns it, what does the published output show while it is unresolved, and what still publishes?
guides.summary: A per-failure-class plan for quarantine, the visible unresolved state and the publication rule, with resolution paths, notification and a rehearsed case.

guides.title: Metric contract
guides.question: What exactly does this metric count, at which grain, with which numerator, denominator, units and reporting period, and how would I catch a wrong computation?
guides.summary: A signed definition of grain, numerator, denominator, units, period and restatement, with tests for double-counting, denominator drift, unit mixing and boundary errors.

guides.title: Slow-workload diagnosis
guides.question: How do I get from "it is slow" to a supported cause, through recorded observations, one refutable hypothesis, a one-variable experiment and a conclusion that says what is still unproven?
guides.summary: A diagnosis record that keeps observation, execution evidence, hypothesis, experiment and conclusion apart, with a correctness check and the production evidence still owed.

guides.title: Dashboard delivery plan
guides.question: Who will act on this page and how, which contract does each number come from, how is freshness stated, who may see it, and how will I prove it shows the right values?
guides.summary: A delivery plan binding each audience to an action and each tile to a metric contract, with freshness in words, an access matrix, a validation script with exact expected values and named owners.

guides.title: Genie benchmark set
guides.question: Which question classes should a natural-language analytics space be tested on, what properties must each answer have, and how are failures reviewed and turned into curation changes?
guides.summary: An authored benchmark of question classes with expected properties and contracted reference answers, a failure classification mapped to curation changes, and a dated run log kept apart from any live-agent claim.

guides.title: Sharing and federation choice
guides.question: Should another party get a copy, a governed share of data that stays in place, or a federated query, judged by movement, authorization, cost in kind, revocation, freshness and failure?
guides.summary: A same-terms comparison of copy, governed share and federation for each direction of one partner need, with the limits of each, a conditional decision per direction and a planned revocation rehearsal.

guides.title: Model evaluation report
guides.question: How do I report a model's target, baselines, split, metrics, risks and monitoring so that a reader can decide whether to use it, including deciding not yet?
guides.summary: An evaluation report that ties target to action, judges the model against the rule in use and a trivial predictor on a deployment-shaped split, reports unseen entities separately and ends in a supported decision.

guides.title: RAG evaluation plan
guides.question: How do I judge whether a retrieval-augmented assistant answers from authorized, current sources and abstains when it should?
guides.summary: A plan that fixes the source set, writes cases before any run, scores retrieval, reasoning and policy separately, and declares the failures that block expansion.

guides.title: Untrusted content threat review
guides.question: Where can untrusted text enter my assistant or pipeline, and which boundaries actually stop it from becoming an instruction or an action?
guides.summary: A review that traces every path untrusted content takes into model context and names the boundary that enforces each control, so a prompt is never counted as a defence.

guides.title: Tool action review
guides.question: Before an assistant can call a tool, what must I establish about identity, scope, approvals, idempotency and audit evidence?
guides.summary: A per-tool card and test matrix that states who acts, what a call may touch, when a human approves, how replays are made safe and what evidence proves it.

guides.title: Application state design
guides.question: For an application on the platform, where does each request go, which contracts bind the pieces, and which state needs transactions?
guides.summary: A design note that walks each important request from browser to data, names contracts and identities at every hop, and classifies state by its transactional needs before choosing storage.

guides.title: Migration inventory
guides.question: What do I need to know about each existing workload, object and consumer before I can choose a safe first migration slice?
guides.summary: An inventory of dependencies, compatibility flags, owners and separately recorded risk axes that ends in a pilot chosen against stated criteria.

guides.title: Reconciliation plan
guides.question: How do I compare an old and a new data path so that keyed differences, totals, nulls and time boundaries are all checked before I accept the result?
guides.summary: A comparison method that aligns the basis first, checks keys before totals, treats nulls and time explicitly, and states thresholds and exceptions before the run.

guides.title: Cutover and rollback plan
guides.question: What must be true before consumers switch to the new path, who decides, what stays running, and how do we prove we can go back?
guides.summary: A plan of verifiable entry conditions, named decision owners, a retained fallback path, observable rollback triggers and a rehearsed recovery test.

guides.title: Demo script
guides.question: How do I script a short demo that answers one business question with verifiable evidence at the right depth for the people in the room?
guides.summary: A script structure that opens with the decision, plans evidence moments the audience can check, asks an explain-back question and sets depth by audience.

guides.title: Demo failure plan
guides.question: What do I do when a live demo step fails so the meeting stays useful and no prepared output is passed off as a live result?
guides.summary: A prepared fallback with labelled local material, an honest explanation script, a troubleshooting time box and the follow-up evidence that returns afterwards.

guides.title: Proof-of-value charter
guides.question: What must a proof-of-value charter fix before execution so that its result can be interpreted afterwards by someone who was not there?
guides.summary: A charter with a measured baseline, one hypothesis, bounded scope, confirmed roles, acceptor-owned criteria, stop conditions and named exit decisions.

guides.title: Evidence ledger
guides.question: How do I keep every claim in an engagement tied to its test, observation, source, caveat and unresolved gap?
guides.summary: One append-only ledger in which each claim carries what was done to test it, what was seen, where the evidence lives and what still stops the row from closing.

guides.title: Cost and value model
guides.question: How do I build a cost and value model whose every input is labelled and whose sensitivity shows which assumption the decision turns on?
guides.summary: A model with labelled inputs (unit, currency, period, source), hand-checkable arithmetic, low/base/high cases, break-even on the deciding driver and an explicit exclusions list.

guides.title: Alternatives memo
guides.question: How do I compare options, including keeping the current path, on neutral criteria with sourced facts and honest unknowns?
guides.summary: A memo that chooses criteria before options, fills cells only with sourced facts or explicit unknowns, refuses scores, and names what would reverse its recommendation.

guides.title: Executive readout
guides.question: How do I give a decision-maker the decision, the evidence, its business meaning and the next step on one page without a score?
guides.summary: A one-page readout that leads with the decision requested, tables each criterion's status and evidence, translates results to business meaning and asks for exactly one approval.

guides.title: Escalation packet
guides.question: How do I write an escalation that a specialist can act on: symptoms, impact, reproduction, sanitized logs and one precise request?
guides.summary: A packet ordered as a specialist reads it, separating observations from hypotheses, counting reproductions, sanitizing evidence and ending with one answerable request and an update time.

guides.title: Handoff and adoption plan
guides.question: What must be true, and who must have agreed, on the day the builders step back from a working path?
guides.summary: A plan of components with acknowledged owners and backups, mapped dependencies, observed readiness items, an adoption path with retirement conditions and dated follow-ups.

labs.title: Python parsing under a contract
labs.summary: Turn a CSV delivery and a JSON delivery from two fictional plants into typed Python values under one small contract, or reject each record with a named reason and its raw input, so that accepted plus rejected equals received; a third plant's transfer delivery breaks the same rules in new ways.
labs.outcome: Parse and validate records with explicit types, tell null from missing from blank from zero, keep rejections with reasons, log without side effects at import, and prove each rule with a test that fails for the stated defect.
labs.environment: Python 3.12 standard library only; nothing to install.
labs.evidence: 36 tests executed locally with zero skips; a shipped mutation check shows fourteen one-line defects each failing a test. Hashes in docs/academy/labs/lab-l01-python-parsing.json.

labs.title: SQL and PySpark equivalence
labs.summary: The same typed synthetic inspection data transformed with Spark SQL and with the DataFrame API; results and types are compared deliberately, including an order-dependent failure and null-handling divergences until corrected.
labs.outcome: Write the same transformation both ways, compare schemas and sorted rows, and explain why implicit row order and null comparisons break equivalence.
labs.environment: Python 3.12, Apache Spark 4.0.4 (PySpark, local[2], UI off), Java 21.
labs.evidence: 9 tests executed locally with zero skips; fixture and output hashes in docs/academy/labs/lab-l02-sql-pyspark-equivalence.json.

labs.title: Join cardinality and weighted metrics
labs.summary: A plausible incorrect total from a multiplying join, its diagnosis by counts and duplicate keys, the repair, a weighted-rate versus average-of-rates trap, a left-join count trap and a transfer test on a different duplicated dimension.
labs.outcome: Detect and repair a multiplying join, compute a weighted metric correctly and read a null-propagating count.
labs.environment: Python 3.12, Apache Spark 4.0.4 (PySpark, local[2], UI off), Java 21.
labs.evidence: 9 tests executed locally with zero skips; hashes in docs/academy/labs/lab-l03-join-cardinality.json.

labs.title: Plans, shuffles and skew
labs.summary: Read the plans Spark prints for a narrow chain, a grouped sum, a sort-merge and a broadcast join, a window, a salted join and a cached filter over a 240-row synthetic feed, predict each expensive boundary, then compare the prediction with the jobs, stages, tasks and shuffle records Spark actually executed, including adaptive coalescing, a runtime join switch and skew splitting.
labs.outcome: Locate exchanges and stage boundaries in an explained plan, explain why a hot key never splits by repartitioning, show that salting spreads it while keeping totals, and tell a plan change from an answer change.
labs.environment: Python 3.12, Apache Spark 4.0.4 (PySpark, local[2], UI off, four shuffle partitions), Java 21; shuffle records read from Spark's status store. No timings are measured.
labs.evidence: 14 tests executed locally with zero skips; expected values come from a plain-Python derivation that never imports Spark. Hashes and the recorded adaptive build sides are in docs/academy/labs/lab-l04-plans-shuffle.json.

labs.title: Delta versions, merges and maintenance on a real table
labs.summary: Move one small open-source Delta table through nine committed versions (a write, an append, a correcting UPDATE, enabling the change data feed, three MERGE statements with different intentions, a schema-evolving append and OPTIMIZE), predict what Delta will report after each, read it back by version, history, detail, change feed and files, and watch four unsafe requests be refused.
labs.outcome: Predict a table's rows at any version, choose the MERGE clauses an incremental or complete delivery needs, keep stale replays out, evolve a schema deliberately and read maintenance from history without deleting data.
labs.environment: Python 3.12, Apache Spark 4.0.4 with open-source delta-spark 4.0.0 (local[2], UI off), Java 21; the first run downloads the Delta jars from Maven Central unless they are already cached. Not Databricks.
labs.evidence: 19 tests executed locally with zero skips; expected rows, history and change-feed entries are hand-derived in DATA.md. Hashes in docs/academy/labs/lab-l05-delta-snapshots.json.

labs.title: Incremental record resolution
labs.summary: Reuse the unchanged Cinderline resolver as a byte-identical reference and apply it to a second plant's raw deliveries: duplicates, late older revisions, valid corrections, conflicting payloads and unkeyed conflicts.
labs.outcome: Predict accepted state, totals, quarantine and the publication decision for changing records, and explain why replay never inflates accepted totals.
labs.environment: Python 3.12 standard library; the reference resolver is pure Python and is hash-checked against the original package.
labs.evidence: 24 tests executed locally with zero skips; fixture and output hashes and the reference SHA-256 are recorded in docs/academy/labs/lab-l06-record-resolution.json.

labs.title: Change events into current and history tables
labs.summary: Turn eighteen fictional part change events, delivered in three batches, into the two tables a change-data pipeline publishes: a current table (one row per key) and a history table (one row per version with a validity interval), under a stated source contract and with the cases that break naive designs: a late arrival, an identical redelivery, a repeated state, a tie on the sequence value, a non-integer sequence and a deleted part that returns.
labs.outcome: State the source contract a change-data flow needs, compute SCD type 1 and type 2 tables with window functions in both the DataFrame API and Spark SQL, and read what a declared AUTO CDC flow would do with the same events.
labs.environment: Local Apache Spark 4.0.4 on one machine (local[2], UI off, UTC) with Python 3.12: no Databricks, no Delta Lake, no declarative pipeline, no network call. PySpark 4.0.4 has no pipelines module, which the runner records; the AUTO CDC adaptation is read, not executed.
labs.evidence: 17 tests executed locally with zero skips: both table computations held to rows written by hand for every planted case, recorded in docs/academy/labs/lab-l07-scd.json.

labs.title: Streaming with event time, a checkpoint and a restart
labs.summary: Run a real Structured Streaming query over five synthetic press-line files: a 10-minute windowed aggregation with a 5-minute watermark, late rows inside and outside the watermark, a checkpoint that records what each micro-batch planned and committed, a restart that neither loses nor duplicates windows, and foreachBatch delivery to two stand-in downstream systems made idempotent.
labs.outcome: Predict which windows a watermark finalizes and which late rows it drops, read a checkpoint's offsets and commits, and explain why a restart is safe only when the sink write is idempotent.
labs.environment: Python 3.12, Apache Spark 4.0.4 Structured Streaming (PySpark, local[2], trigger availableNow, no sleeps), Java 21; stand-in sinks append to local lists.
labs.evidence: 13 tests executed locally with zero skips; batch results are also re-derived by a plain-Python script that never imports Spark. Hashes in docs/academy/labs/lab-l08-streaming-restart.json.

labs.title: Failure and recovery boundaries in a four-task pipeline
labs.summary: Break a fictional four-task daily report pipeline (retain the export, resolve lots, publish the report, notify two recipients) at four injected points and recover by re-running the same run id: succeeded tasks are reused, the failed task and its successors run again, and an idempotency key keeps a notification from going out twice. A stale input that turns every task green is refused by a freshness check.
labs.outcome: Explain why a green task is a statement about its own success condition, not about the business data, and design keys, a ledger and a freshness check so a retry or a backfill can never duplicate an effect or move the current report.
labs.environment: Python 3.12 standard library on one machine: no scheduler service, no Lakeflow Jobs run, no Databricks workspace and no network. Failures are injected by raising an exception at a named point; the only external effect appends to a Python list, and no message is ever sent.
labs.evidence: 43 tests executed locally with zero skips; the filled starter passes 41 of 41 in starter mode and the package's mutation check catches 14 of 14 deliberate defects. Recorded in docs/academy/labs/lab-l09-failure-recovery.json.

labs.title: Data contracts and quarantine
labs.summary: Validate schema, keys, quantities and cross-record constraints over synthetic inspection deliveries, quarantine rows with reasons, and show why row-level checks cannot establish uniqueness or completeness on their own.
labs.outcome: Write a contract-driven validator, read a quarantine by reason, and separate row-level validity from multi-row and source-completeness evidence.
labs.environment: Python 3.12 standard library.
labs.evidence: 19 tests executed locally with zero skips, including a permissive validator that fails for the asserted reason; hashes in docs/academy/labs/lab-l10-contracts-quarantine.json.

labs.title: Model it, then contract the metric
labs.summary: Build a small star schema from synthetic accepted inspections (one fact at the grain of one inspection; line, plant, shift and date dimensions; supervisor history as type 2 rows), compute a unit defect rate at line-day, plant-day and plant-month from a metric contract, then watch five deliberately broken queries fail for their stated reasons.
labs.outcome: Declare a fact's grain, keep type 2 history joinable at a point in time, compute a ratio metric from summed numerator and denominator at any level, and recognize averaging of rates, many-to-many double counts and calendar-window mismatches.
labs.environment: Python 3.12, Apache Spark 4.0.4 (PySpark, local[2], UI off, session time zone UTC), Java 21; no Unity Catalog object or metric view.
labs.evidence: 20 tests executed locally with zero skips; running them with --sql starters/model.sql against the unfilled starter shows most fail until the gaps are filled. Hashes in docs/academy/labs/lab-l11-modeling-metrics.json.

labs.title: Time-aware analytical SQL
labs.summary: A Spark SQL portfolio over five synthetic plant files: window frames, ranking and deduplication, gaps and islands, membership with EXISTS versus IN and NULLs, set operations, nested fields, safe casts under ANSI mode and daylight-saving-time arithmetic, with every expected value written down before the query ran.
labs.outcome: Predict a window's rows and a query's result row by row, choose the membership form that survives NULLs, cast defensively, and state which time zone a timestamp calculation used.
labs.environment: Python 3.12, Apache Spark 4.0.4 (PySpark, local[2], UI off, ANSI mode on, session time zone America/New_York), Java 21.
labs.evidence: 51 tests executed locally with zero skips; time-zone answers come from an independent zoneinfo script that never touches Spark. Hashes in docs/academy/labs/lab-l12-time-aware-sql.json.

labs.title: A reproducible cost worksheet and a controlled cost experiment
labs.summary: Build a cost worksheet a reader can recompute: six cost drivers in their own units and periods with explicitly hypothetical rates, restated per month in one currency across low, base and high cases, the one-off migration kept apart and the most sensitive input named; then turn synthetic run observations into cost per unit of work and refuse the rows that cannot honestly be divided.
labs.outcome: Keep units, periods and currency explicit, compare only comparable alternatives, find the input that moves the answer most, and compute cost per unit of work with named refusals instead of guesses.
labs.environment: Python 3.12 standard library only; every rate is a labelled hypothetical rate, not a price.
labs.evidence: 30 tests executed locally with zero skips; expected values are derived independently in DATA.md. Hashes in docs/academy/labs/lab-l13-cost-model.json.

labs.title: Governance review: access decisions, filters and masks
labs.summary: A tabletop review of a fictional principal, object and action matrix: predict who may do what and which check decides (USE CATALOG and USE SCHEMA before SELECT, deny by default, ownership, inherited privileges), what a row filter and a column mask return for each caller, and which negative cases a review must test; a small local evaluator checks the answers against hand-written keys.
labs.outcome: Read an access table the way Unity Catalog evaluates it, predict filtered and masked results per caller, and design the negative tests an access review needs.
labs.environment: Worked on paper or in an editor; answers are checked by a Python 3.12 standard-library evaluator. A locally evaluated policy table is not Unity Catalog enforcement: no GRANT, filter, mask, ABAC policy, authentication or audit query was executed.
labs.evidence: 23 tests executed locally with zero skips against hand-written answer keys; the seven platform steps that were not executed are listed in docs/academy/labs/lab-l14-governance-review.json.

labs.title: Deliver a job as a reviewed package and bundle
labs.summary: Turn a fictional daily scrap-rate job, once a hand-copied notebook with a pasted token, into a small Python package with its own unit tests and a Declarative Automation Bundle (formerly Databricks Asset Bundles) with dev, test and prod targets. Local checks parse the bundle, apply 21 structure rules, resolve each target's configuration and run the package tests; every Databricks step is named and left not run.
labs.outcome: Explain what each delivery state proves (local source, validation, reviewed artifact, deployment, execution), keep environment differences in configuration, and read a bundle's targets the way validate and deploy would.
labs.environment: Python 3.12 with PyYAML 6.0.3 on one machine. The Databricks CLI and SDK are not installed, no workspace is contacted and no token exists; the test runner refuses network connections and subprocesses.
labs.evidence: 16 local tests executed with zero skips (including the package's 14 unit tests), recorded in docs/academy/labs/lab-l16-bundle-delivery.json. Authentication, bundle validate, plan, deploy, run, integration tests and promotion are listed as NOT RUN.

labs.title: A baseline, a tracked experiment and an evidence-based promotion
labs.summary: Predict a coating-oven fault stop from a small seeded synthetic dataset: a naive baseline and a simple model, a leaking split exposed and corrected by time, comparable runs tracked in open-source MLflow with parameters, metrics, dataset digests and signatures, an impressive run that cannot be reproduced, a model contract that refuses schema drift and a promotion decision that reads the evidence before the metrics.
labs.outcome: Compare a model with a baseline under a time-based split, record runs so a result can be rerun exactly, enforce a model's input contract and justify or refuse a promotion from its evidence.
labs.environment: Python 3.12 with MLflow 3.16.1, scikit-learn 1.9.1, pandas 3.0.6, numpy 2.5.3, scipy 1.18.1 and skops 0.15.0; MLflow tracks into a file store in a temporary directory; no tracking server, Unity Catalog or network.
labs.evidence: 32 tests executed locally with zero skips; expected metrics come from an independent derivation script, and the temporary tracking store is deleted. Hashes in docs/academy/labs/lab-l17-baseline-mlflow.json.

labs.title: Point-in-time features
labs.summary: Build a feature table from timestamped sensor readings whose two-hour windows publish thirty minutes after they close, join it to labelled prediction times as of what was actually known, and prove that future readings, duplicate entity-time rows and a drifted serving transform are all rejected.
labs.outcome: Construct a point-in-time-correct training set, name the leak in event-time and latest-value shortcuts, catch training/serving skew with a consistency check, and explain which predictions change when late readings append new feature versions.
labs.environment: Python 3.12 with pandas 3.0.6 and numpy 2.5.3; no Spark, Java, MLflow or network.
labs.evidence: 25 tests executed locally with zero skips, including shortcut starters that fail for their documented reason; hashes in docs/academy/labs/lab-l18-point-in-time-features.json.

labs.title: Forecasts, anomaly thresholds and a ranked queue
labs.summary: Three decisions on a fictional production line that each get called prediction and each need their own evaluation: a weekly unit forecast judged by rolling-origin backtests against naive and seasonal baselines, an anomaly score for daily defect counts with a threshold table that prices every flag, and a ranked inspection queue judged by precision at k.
labs.outcome: Choose the horizon, the baseline and the backtest before the model; read an interval and an anomaly threshold as costs; and rank a queue by the metric the shift can act on.
labs.environment: pandas 3.0.6, numpy 2.5.3 and scikit-learn 1.9.1 on Python 3.12, one machine, CPU only, no network: no Spark, no Databricks, no AutoML and no model service.
labs.evidence: 41 tests executed locally with zero skips against literals derived independently in the standard library, including the fixture checked byte for byte and six deliberate shortcuts shown to fail, recorded in docs/academy/labs/lab-l19-forecast-anomaly.json.

labs.title: Retrieval quality on a governed lexical baseline
labs.summary: Build a small TF-IDF retriever over eighteen fictional maintenance documents with version, effective date, plant and audience metadata. Compare two chunk sizes, filter by permission before ranking, prefer current revisions, measure recall@k and MRR on labelled questions, and watch the wrong chunk win, a newer authorized source change the answer and an unauthorized document stay out.
labs.outcome: Evaluate retrieval separately from answer quality, place the permission filter before ranking, handle superseded and region-restricted documents, and explain why a lexical baseline fails where it does.
labs.environment: Python 3.12 with scikit-learn 1.9.1 (TfidfVectorizer), numpy and scipy; lexical retrieval only: no neural embeddings, no vector index, no Databricks AI Search, no network.
labs.evidence: 28 tests executed locally with zero skips; expected relevant chunks are authored per question. Hashes in docs/academy/labs/lab-l20-retrieval-quality.json.

labs.title: Evaluation harness, traces and a failure taxonomy
labs.summary: Build a deterministic evaluation harness for a fictional read-only maintenance assistant: twelve cases with expected properties written before any answer exists, six scorers for citations, abstention, forbidden tools and required fields, a classifier that reads each trace span by span and names the failure (retrieval, reasoning, denied tool, policy block), and a deliberately lenient citation scorer rejected against reference verdicts.
labs.outcome: State expected properties before evaluating, score them deterministically, locate a failure in a trace, validate a scorer before trusting it, and reuse the harness on a second domain.
labs.environment: Python 3.12 standard library only; answers and traces are authored fixtures, not model outputs, and no model, hosted judge or endpoint is called.
labs.evidence: 33 tests executed locally with zero skips, including a lenient scorer that fails for its asserted reason. Hashes in docs/academy/labs/lab-l21-evaluation-traces.json.

labs.title: Tool calls behind an application-side policy gate
labs.summary: Build the policy gate between a fictional maintenance assistant and three local stand-ins for real systems. It decides each scripted tool proposal from the signed-in user's session, the exposed tools and their schemas, the user's grants intersected with the application's delegated scopes, an idempotency key and an approval policy, and writes one audit row per decision. Twenty scripted proposals and five approval actions, some carrying instructions injected into retrieved documents, attack it.
labs.outcome: Explain why a model's proposal is not an authorization, and implement and test the checks an application makes before a tool call has any effect: identity, schema, delegated permission, idempotent retries, human approval and audit.
labs.environment: Python 3.12 standard library on one machine: no packages, no network, no language model, no MCP server and no Databricks workspace. Scripted proposals stand in for a model, and every effect is an append to an in-memory list.
labs.evidence: 41 tests executed locally with zero skips against hand-written expected decisions, effects and audit rows; the package's mutation check catches all nine deliberate gate defects. Recorded in docs/academy/labs/lab-l22-tool-authorization.json.

labs.title: Transactional state for a quality-review app
labs.summary: Constraints, an idempotent at-least-once intake, a work queue claimed with FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED across two real sessions, optimistic concurrency with a version column, isolation timelines and a least-privilege application role, all on a local PostgreSQL 16 server, plus a Lakebase adaptation guide kept separate from what ran.
labs.outcome: Design operational state that survives redelivery and concurrent reviewers, show why an unlocked read-then-update double-claims and last-write-wins loses a decision, and list what a managed Lakebase deployment would still need to prove.
labs.environment: Python 3.12 standard library driving a throwaway local PostgreSQL 16 server (initdb, pg_ctl, psql) on 127.0.0.1; managed Lakebase, OAuth, the pooler and synced tables were not executed.
labs.evidence: 18 tests executed locally against PostgreSQL 16.13 with zero skips; ten Lakebase platform steps are listed as not executed in docs/academy/labs/lab-l23-transactional-state.json.

labs.title: Migrate a nightly job and reconcile it row by row
labs.summary: Translate a fictional SQL Server stored procedure and SSIS-style package into Spark SQL job tasks and prove, row by row against hand-authored legacy outputs, where the translation keeps or changes meaning: collation and trailing spaces, predicates in a LEFT JOIN's ON clause, the business-day clock, integer division, exact money, watermarks and a parallel-run cutover gate.
labs.outcome: Inventory legacy logic before translating, reproduce legacy meaning with explicit choices, reconcile keyed differences, totals and NULLs, and decide a cutover from parallel-run evidence rather than from row counts.
labs.environment: Python 3.12, Apache Spark 4.0.4 (PySpark, local[2], UI off), Java 21; no SQL Server, SSIS or Agent instance, and no Databricks workspace.
labs.evidence: 28 tests executed locally with zero skips; the legacy outputs are hand-authored fixtures derived in DATA.md. Hashes in docs/academy/labs/lab-l24-migration-reconciliation.json.
